transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-24 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Platform: Zoom (recording available)
- Attendees listed in metadata

Summary:
Redwood team walked Ironclad Labs through the Console per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and cost attribution. Focus on how to map endpoints/routes to product features for chargeback and FinOps, plus a short discussion on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment (VPC), SSO/KMS concerns, and a proposed POC to run their 3 representative prompts.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and tagging
- Cost decomposition (tokens, GPU time, model variant routing)
- Batching and caching suggestions from Optimize
- Security (SOC2, KMS, VPC) and data residency
- POC scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, we can give a quick peek at the console — hey Samir, can you still hear me?
[00:04] Samir Patel: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:06] Diego Alvarez: hi all, Diego from Redwood infra, I’ll cover the per-route dive and the cost breakdown.
[00:12] Evelyn Ross: thanks, we only have about 50 minutes, so show us the parts that matter to finance first — per-route cost and exportable reports.
[00:20] Maya Chen: totally. quick context, Ironclad mentioned you have three main product routes: chat customer, summarization batch, and realtime transcription — is that right?
[00:28] Jon Kim: yes roughly, the realtime transcription is the heaviest latency sensitive route.
[00:32] Maya Chen: ok great. I’ll pull up the Console, you might see the main usage dashboard — sometimes the recording auto labels it as Redwood "Consol" (laughs) — ignore that.
[00:40] [00:40] Diego Alvarez: 
- (screen) so this is the Route view, each row is a route you register with tags. we show 7-day trends, token volume, avg latency, and a per-token unit cost estimate. note these are model-level approximations, then we apply the runtime delta for GPU time.
[01:12] Evelyn Ross: is that unit cost raw tokens * model price? or does it include batching and reserved capacity effects?
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: good question. base unit is tokens * model list price. then our telemetry adds actual runtime multiplier — so if you run on dedicated pools with optimized kernels you’ll see a lower runtime multiplier. the Console also surfaces batching efficiency and prefix cache hits which reduce effective tokens. sometimes the transcriber hears KV "cash" instead of KV cache in transcripts, so that’s fun.
[01:40] Priya Nair: for security we need to know where logs live. do you keep token payloads in the control plane?
[01:46] Maya Chen: short answer, by default we store request metadata and trace IDs in our control plane, but payloads are redacted unless you opt-in for debug. for Private (VPC or on-prem) the control plane can be customer-managed and logs land in your KMS-backed storage. we have a SOC2 report and a short checklist — I’ll send that after the call.
[02:10] Jon Kim: on the runtime multiplier, can you show an example where two routes hit same model but cost differs?
[02:16] Diego Alvarez: sure — here's chat-customer hitting a 13B model at short context length, with high prefix reuse so cache hit is 60%. avg latency 180ms; cost per 1k tokens shows at ~$0.28 after batching. compare that to realtime-transcribe which pins to a low-latency profile, no caching, smaller batch windows — runtime multiplier is higher so effective cost ~ $0.45 per 1k tokens.
[02:46] Samir Patel: that delta is useful. do you show per-account or per-team breakdowns for chargeback?
[02:52] Diego Alvarez: yes we have route tags that map to teams/products, you can slice by tag, by model, by region. export CSVs and our billing API emits per-route usage lines that match your billing system.
[03:10] Evelyn Ross: can this be ingested straight into our chargeback system? we use internal accounting tool that expects per-minute cost lines.
[03:16] Maya Chen: absolutely — our billing export has line items with timestamp, route_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, runtime_ms, and cost_usd. Diego, there's a sample export?
[03:26] Diego Alvarez: yeah, sample export link in the console, and we'll attach a sample schema.
[03:30] [03:30] Maya Chen: 
- quick aside, we often recommend a per-route SLA tag so finance knows which endpoints can absorb higher costs for latency SLOs.
[03:44] Jon Kim: about model_variant — we sometimes fallback to smaller models. is that automatic or policy-based?
[03:50] Diego Alvarez: routing is policy-based. you define policies: prefer low-cost variant, or prefer low-latency, and we do smart routing. if capacity is constrained we can fallback to a quantized variant. Console logs the exact route decision so you can audit when fallbacks happen.
[04:08] Samir Patel: any notes on tokenization differences? we saw differences between your metrics and an openai billing export previously.
[04:14] Diego Alvarez: tokenization can diverge between encoders; our billing uses the tokenizer from the model artifact we serve. if you have a reconciliation mismatch we can run a quick job to re-tokenize sample payloads and show mapping.
[04:26] Priya Nair: encryption at rest — we require KMS integration and HSM for keys. is that available for Private?
[04:32] Maya Chen: yes, Private supports customer KMS and HSM via standard integrations; Hosted can use our managed KMS but we offer BYOK for enterprise.
[04:40] [04:40] Diego Alvarez: back to the UI — clicking into a route opens the timeseries: top pane is token volume, middle is latency distribution, bottom is cost decomposition (model price, runtime premium, caching savings). you can hover to see the raw data.
[05:10] Evelyn Ross: show me a trend where batching helped reduce cost.
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: here's an example — we toggled continuous batching for a demo route, batching increased from 20% to 70%, effective cost dropped by ~32% over the week. note: batching tradeoff is extra latency; we provide percentiles.
[05:34] Jon Kim: what's the typical lat penalty for batching at 70%?
[05:38] Diego Alvarez: depends on traffic shape; at 70% we saw the p95 increase by 40-80ms in our examples. for chat routes that's often acceptable; for realtime transcription you'd keep batching low or use the low-latency pool.
[05:54] Samir Patel: what about Optimize recommendations — can the Console suggest batching thresholds automatically?
[05:59] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Optimize generates suggested batch size, cache TTL, and quantization profile per route based on your traffic. it shows estimated cost savings and potential quality impact for each suggestion.
[06:12] [06:12] Evelyn Ross: and those suggestions can be approved by a gate? we need human approval before impacting production.
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: suggestions live in a review queue; you can stage them to a canary route or apply automatically with an approval policy.
[06:26] Jon Kim: on canaries — can we do A/B with a percentage split?
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: yes, route rollouts support percentage splits, model variants, and fallback policies. Console shows live split telemetry so you can compare quality and cost.
[06:40] [06:40] Maya Chen: 
- quick poll, who owns the chargeback mapping at Ironclad? Evelyn?
[06:44] Evelyn Ross: yep that's me.
[06:46] Maya Chen: ok Evelyn we can share a template CSV that maps your internal cost centers to route tags and show a mock chargeback run.
[06:52] Evelyn Ross: perfect.
[06:54] Samir Patel: timeline question — we want the POC in the next two weeks if possible. is that realistic?
[06:59] Diego Alvarez: yes, if we have the 3 prompts and traffic profile we can spin a dedicated sandbox pool for 48-72 hours and run the benchmarks. we’ll need your sample prompts and desired SLOs.
[07:12] Maya Chen: I’ll include a POC checklist. Diego will own the perf runbook.
[07:16] [07:16] Jon Kim: security: Priya asked about audit logs and SSO — we use Okta. how's SAML integration?
[07:22] Maya Chen: we have SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, whatever). for Private deployments logs can be forwarded to your collectors behind the VPC.
[07:36] Priya Nair: how long do you keep request traces by default?
[07:39] Diego Alvarez: default retention for traces is 90 days; you can change that with an enterprise retention policy. traces can be redacted to remove PII.
[07:50] Samir Patel: ok can you show the export UI?
[07:52] Diego Alvarez: clicking Billing -> Exports -> New export. select time window, route tags, and export type CSV or Parquet. you can schedule recurring exports to S3 or push to our billing API. example showed earlier.
[08:12] Evelyn Ross: about recurring, does it support daily deltas vs full snapshots?
[08:16] Diego Alvarez: yes we have delta mode which emits only new lines since last export.
[08:20] [08:20] Maya Chen: 
- note on region routing: if you want to keep data in eu-west-1 we can pin model serving to that region and reflect region-level cost differences in the Console.
[08:34] Jon Kim: do model variants in different regions have different kernel perf? like NVLink pooled GPUs vs local?
[08:38] Diego Alvarez: yes hardware and kernel combos change runtime; Console shows a region multiplier spotlight.
[08:44] Samir Patel: competitor question — we've been testing Anthropic and OpenAI for latency. how do you compare on per-token cost and tail latency?
[08:51] Maya Chen: it depends on model class. our Console is model-agnostic, we show cost delta relative to the model list price and runtime. we also have Redwood-verified performance profiles for common open models which we can share.
[09:06] Evelyn Ross: ok we need the SOC2 and the Private deployment checklist.
[09:10] Maya Chen: will send after call.
[09:14] [09:14] Diego Alvarez: 
- jumping to anomaly detection: Console flags sudden token spikes or model fallbacks; it can create an alert that pages an on-call or opens a ticket in Jira.
[09:30] Jon Kim: can alerts be for cost thresholds too?
[09:33] Diego Alvarez: yep, cost threshold, rate of spend increase, or per-route P95 crossing. alerts can be routed to Slack, pagerduty, or email.
[09:44] Samir Patel: about the POC, what do we need to commit on Redwood side?
[09:48] Maya Chen: we’ll provision a sandbox project, allocate dedicated capacity for the benchmark window, and share an estimated cost for the sandbox. Diego will set up the test harness.
[09:58] Evelyn Ross: estimate would help us get internal approval.
[10:01] Maya Chen: we'll include that in the pricing email.
[10:04] [10:04] Diego Alvarez: 
- quick note on quality regressions: we have evals tied to prompt sets; during POC we can run pre/post evals to confirm no regression when switching quantization or batching.
[10:20] Priya Nair: who signs the data processing addendum? our legal team will need to review.
[10:24] Maya Chen: we have a standard DPA, and an addendum for Private with additional controls — legal is used to reviewing these, I'll introduce our legal contact.
[10:34] Samir Patel: anything else on the Console features?
[10:36] Diego Alvarez: one more: rate-limited sampling view — it shows token-level cost per route during traffic bursts, helpful for spike forensics.
[10:44] Jon Kim: ok good.
[10:46] Maya Chen: to recap: we showed per-route dashboards, exports, Optimize suggestions, and POC plan. next steps: Maya to send pricing + SOC2 + POC checklist, Diego to own perf runbook, Samir to share prompts.
[10:58] Evelyn Ross: sounds good, we’ll aim to send prompts tomorrow.
[11:02] Samir Patel: thanks everyone.
[11:04] Maya Chen: thanks, will follow up with the spreadsheet and link to the recorded session.

(End of recording)
